leverage.exposure: No leverage is open and none should be opened. The balance is positive, and it must still be positive when the matchday starts, because a negative balance at the lock scores nothing at all for the entire matchday. Both of this run's tempting buys would have breached that — one narrowly and only until the Amoako sale settled, the other by a margin no realistic sequence of sales could close. Spending remains capped by the value floor rather than by the balance, but neither cap is the operative constraint this run, because there is nothing worth buying.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is not a missing position but an unplaced player. Twelve are owned and eleven are placed, and the man left out is the wrong one — the current shape fields two players who are near-certain zeros while benching a defender his club's probable eleven has starting. Fixing that costs nothing, requires no transfer and no cash, and is worth more than anything the market is offering. Behind it, the real structural limit is that only one sale is legally available before the squad falls below a fillable shape, which is why the choice of which player to sell is forced rather than free.

verdict.detail: No action changed since the last run. The top move is still free and still unexecuted: fix the lineup to 5-3-2 with Bernardo in and Amoako out, and only then sell Amoako. This run's news sweep strengthens that plan rather than altering it — Ligainsider's Hoffenheim page, updated today, names Bernardo at left-back for Matchday 2, his fitness flag is green, and the liveticker for his Matchday 1 substitution records no injury notation at all. The Kickbase status flag on him is now contradicted by three independent dated checks. The board produced two new arrivals and neither is buyable. Nothing on the market improves the eleven, so the cash has nothing to convert into this cycle and the right posture is patience until the last runs before the Friday lock.

sell.reason: Amoako remains the only points-free sale on the books and the case is unchanged. Ligainsider's Hamburg page has him in the full squad but neither in the starting eleven nor on the bench for the trip to Mainz, he is absent from the injury and suspension table, and he took no minutes at all on Matchday 1. This is a selection verdict, not a fitness one. He is also decaying fast in value, so waiting costs money as well as nothing gained. Critically, the sale must follow the lineup fix, not precede it: once he is gone the squad is eleven and every man must be placed, so selling first can strand the team in an unfilled shape and a penalty. Lokonga and Widmer both stay held for structure — Lokonga is the worst points-per-euro in the squad and Widmer is a confirmed non-starter, but with only one sale legally available, selling either instead of Amoako costs fielded points.

standing.name: Amoako

The squad is 12, so a sale is legal for the first time - it takes him to 11 = 1/5/3/2, which fills 5-3-2. Selling Widmer instead forces Amoako back in and costs 29; selling Bernardo instead costs 62 (see the companion HOLD). NEWS, DATED AND FRESH THIS RUN: Ligainsider HSV probable XI, page last updated 01.09.2026 20:31 (after MD1), for the 06.09 trip to Mainz - Amoako appears ONLY in the full squad roster, NOT among the starters and NOT on the bench. He is not on Ligainsider Verletzte-und-Gesperrte (HSV's absentees are Omari, Dickes, Roessing-Lelesiit), so this is a selection verdict, not an injury: he is fit and simply not in the picture. Kickbase gives him no p and no ap field at all - zero points, zero minutes across MD1. VALUE, SECOND REASON: mvt 2 falling, sdmvt -882.669/day, tfhmvt -116.705/2h. Over the 45,6h to the lock that is roughly another 1,7M of decay on a 1,7M asset - selling now captures nearly all of what is left. Georg bought him at +79,18% over mv, the third-highest premium in the measured log, and is -1.790.553 on him; that loss is SUNK and is not a reason to hold a player who produces nothing. WHY THE 12th BODY IS NOT WORTH KEEPING AS INSURANCE, priced honestly: the German window shut 2026-09-01T18:00Z, so no squad player can be deleted before MD2 and the -100 deletion risk is dead. The other thing a 12th body buys is the option to bench Bernardo via 4-4-2 - but that option is worth ZERO points, because 4-4-2 without Bernardo is 1333 and 5-3-2 with a non-playing Bernardo is also 1333. The option only pays if there is someone GOOD to field instead, and there is not. SEQUENCING: set the lineup to 5-3-2 BEFORE selling, or the post-sale squad of 11 has only 10 placed. Not urgent against a deadline - it has until the 2026-09-04T18:30Z lock - but every two hours costs ~117k.

buy.reason: Nothing on the board is buyable. Two players arrived since the last run and both were logged as avoids. Borna Sosa is a deadline-day loan from Crystal Palace announced on the first of September, so he has no Bundesliga minutes for Köln, and his coach pointed to Gideon Mensah at left-back while calling Sosa an option — Ligainsider's probable eleven has Mensah starting and Sosa on the bench. He is also priced above available cash, so buying him would open leverage and would only become clean after the Amoako sale. That is the Amoako pattern repeated at a higher price. Guéla Doué is the more painful pass: a genuine deadline-day signing from Strasbourg on a five-year deal, already penciled into Leverkusen's back line for Matchday 2. He is simply unaffordable by a wide margin, and no combination of sales reaches him without gutting the eleven. The rest of the board is the same stale inventory rejected on previous runs. One calibration note stands: the earlier doctrine of bidding the high end of the clearing band is over-fitted and was measured to have overpaid on the Onyeka listing, which drew no competing offers at all. Check the offer count before ever bidding above market value.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There are no manager asks priced below market value anywhere on the board, so the mechanism that would make a flip profitable is simply absent. What did happen is more of the rivals' micro-flipping: one manager bought and re-sold Bouanani within half an hour, and another bought and re-sold Itten sixteen seconds apart. Both were captured in the ledger and both moved the measured flip band by almost nothing. This is motion, not points, and it remains explicitly not a model to copy — every one of those trades used a transfer slot to buy a player who would never be fielded.

fitness.sweep: The league-wide injury and suspension table lists none of the twelve. Bernardo is the headline and the news is good: fit, in the probable eleven at left-back, with the only negative item about him a stale one from February. The one genuinely new concern is Min-jae. He was the incumbent centre-back on Matchday 1, started, played to the eighty-first minute and scored well, and there is no dated item since saying he was dropped, rested or injured — but two dated Matchday 2 predictions leave him out for a rotated pairing, and he is pencilled into a midweek cup start. Call it a coin-flip rather than a benching. It is deliberately not actionable: the optimal shape fields every defender, and the alternative shape that drops him forces a zero-scoring midfielder into the eleven instead, so the two are a wash. Re-check him on the runs inside the final twelve hours before the lock. Widmer is confirmed on the bench at Mainz with da Costa ahead of him, which is known and already priced in — his only current news is his international retirement, and the breathing-difficulty items about him are from last April and stale.
